I am 66 years old, and I have worked this land in Quzhou County for 50 years. I never went to school, but I learned farming from my father, and I know my 8.7 mu better than I know my own hands. My wife and I are the only ones farming now, so every decision must be practical and save labor where it can. We follow the wheat-maize rotation because that is what the North China Plain demands—winter wheat from autumn to early June, then summer maize planted immediately after harvest until autumn.

Right now it is early spring, and the wheat I planted last autumn is greening up. I will topdress nitrogen on it when the soil warms, and I will irrigate it three times: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I use improved wheat seed from the county supply shop, and I rotary tilled the land before planting last autumn. I watch for aphids and rust, and if they appear, I will spray twice. I expect about 450 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather does not turn bad.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will waste no time. I will plant hybrid maize—Zhengdan 958 or another reliable hybrid from the shop—directly into the wheat stubble using no-tillage seeding. There are only a few days between harvest and planting, and at my age I cannot afford to spend energy tilling. I will fertilize the maize with nitrogen, phosphate, and some potash, and irrigate twice: at silking and during grain filling. I will spray for weeds and pests twice. My well gives me water, so I am not at the mercy of the rain, but I do not waste a drop. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the maize.
